blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Rank counts only communities with at least ten homes listed. Falling listings with steady sales mean homes are being absorbed faster; rising listings with steady sales mean more choice for buyers. A sellers’ best bet is a community where homes sell quickly against the number listed; a buyers’ best bet is the reverse. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

blocks.text: Between June 2026 and October 2026, detached houses: listings fell from 87 in June to 84 in October (−3.4%), and it took 14.3% of the city’s 294 sales over the period; condos and townhomes: listings fell from 143 in June to 115 in October (−19.6%), and it took 23.5% of the city’s 456 sales over the period.

The monthly write-ups singled out King George Corridor for detached houses in June (a sellers’ best bet); detached houses in October (a buyers’ best bet); condos and townhomes in September (a sellers’ best bet).

blocks.text: Lots and land in King George Corridor
What trades here

items.t: Lot fabric: detached houses on side streets off the boulevard; low-rise condos and townhomes near the Semiahmoo Town Centre south end; duplex and fourplex-style homes fronting the boulevard; and manufactured homes in the corridor's South Surrey communities. The plan framework concentrates multiple-residential and commercial designations at the town-centre south end and along the boulevard, with lower-density residential behind it.

Fee-simple lots are the default form: a side-street house lot here is fee-simple — no strata corporation, no Form B, no strata fees; diligence is title, the parcel's zone and designation in COSMOS, and the floodplain check at the north end.

A bare-land strata lot is strata tenure on the lot itself — the buyer owns the strata lot (essentially the building lot) and the house on it, and Form B, strata fees for common property and registered bylaws apply to the lot; it is not fee-simple.
Manufactured-home ground is not a bare-land offering
No individual assembly parcel, development site or rezoning application in the corridor is documented, and none is carried as inventory.
A specific parcel's reserve status is checked on the ALC maps by PID or civic address before any farm-use or subdivision assumption is made.
Developer product in this corridor sells built homes under REDMA.

Floodplain at the north end: the corridor's north edge is the Nicomekl River, and Surrey's coastal floodplain runs along the Nicomekl and Serpentine Rivers and the Serpentine–Nicomekl lowlands. Parcel-level flood levels: confirmed with the City per parcel.

The corridor's land value question is the Frequent Bus Stop Area layer, not the street name. Eligible lots within 400 m of a frequent bus stop can carry up to 6 units under SSMUH — two otherwise identical side-street lots can sit in different unit counts because one is inside that layer. Check COSMOS before pricing either.
The attached market here is the liquid side, and it is not land. SnapStats publishes no land category, so that pace says nothing about lot sales; it is community context only.

The City is building Nicomekl Riverfront Park along the river's south bank at the corridor's north end — the same end where the floodplain check applies; amenity and flood diligence arrive together on north-end parcels.

faq.q: Is "King George Corridor" land the whole boulevard, including Whalley?
faq.a: No. On this page, in the City plan and in the board data it is the south segment only — 8 Avenue to the Nicomekl River in South Surrey. A Newton or City Centre parcel on the same road is a different sub-area with different numbers.

faq.q: Can I buy a vacant building lot in the corridor?
faq.a: What trades as land is the existing fabric — side-street house lots, boulevard-fronting lots priced on added-unit potential, and teardown houses at land value — each checked parcel by parcel in COSMOS.

faq.q: Which plan sets what my lot can become?
faq.a: The Surrey 2050 OCP (Bylaw No. 21900, adopted Jun 15, 2026). The corridor's 1995 concept-plan designations were superseded by the OCP update carried through Corporate Report R246 (endorsed Dec 2, 2024) — check the parcel's current designation and zone, not the 1995 plan.

faq.q: Can a house lot here add units?
faq.a: Under SSMUH, most eligible lots under 4,050 m² inside the Urban Containment Boundary carry 3 units (under 280 m²) or 4 units (280 m² or more), and eligible lots within 400 m of a frequent bus stop can carry up to 6 — boulevard-adjacent lots may qualify. That is added-unit permission, not subdivision.

faq.q: Can I subdivide a corridor lot?
faq.a: Only if each new lot meets its zone's minimum subdivision lot area in Bylaw No. 12000 and the subdivision/servicing requirements under the Surrey Subdivision and Development Bylaw, 1986, No. 8830 — confirmed with the City for the specific parcel.

faq.q: Does "King George Corridor" mean the whole boulevard to City Centre?
faq.a: The plan area and sub-area run from 8 Avenue to the Nicomekl River in South Surrey, bordered by Highway 99 to the east; the boulevard continues north through Newton to City Centre, but those stretches — and the Whalley towers — sit in other sub-areas with different numbers.

faq.q: Can a duplex on the corridor also have a suite?
faq.a: Surrey permits one secondary suite per single-family, semi-detached or duplex dwelling unit, at most 40% of the principal unit's habitable floor area, and never inside a coach house or garden suite. Suite legality is a per-parcel check.
